plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. Since I win only if I have the highest bid and pay the second-highest bid, bidding exactly my value ensures I capture all profitable opportunities (winning whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid) while never overpaying. With a value of $48, I will bid my true value to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and lose otherwise (avoiding loss). Since this is a one-shot game with independent private values, there's no reason to shade my bid up or down. I'll bid exactly my value of $6 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $40 to maximize expected profit.
